commands.review_summary:
Adds a ten-second deadline around Slack startup identity validation and regression coverage for continuing through the existing degraded startup path when `auth.test` stalls.

PR surface: Source 0, Tests +44. Total +44 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: no. executed current-main failure transcript was supplied, but the reproduction path is high-confidence: current main directly awaits a WebClient request whose transport timeout defaults to zero, and the controlled head proof demonstrates the same withheld-header stall.

target.title: fix(slack): add timeout to startup auth.test requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users starting a Slack account could wait indefinitely when the startup `auth.test` call stalled.

## Why This Change Was Made

Slack startup now bounds the boot-time `auth.test` wait with the existing shared timeout helper and keeps the current degraded startup path when that identity check fails. The change is limited to startup identity validation and does not alter Slack send, upload, or read lookup behavior.

This is an AI-assisted contribution prepared for Alix-007.

## User Impact

A stalled Slack identity check no longer prevents the Slack provider from reaching the existing degraded startup path and logging the same required-mention warning.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `bd1e78af217d16fcb20124042d896ec23aaf53d5`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/slack/src/monitor/provider.auth-test-token.test.ts --reporter verbose`
- Result: 1 test file passed, 8 tests passed in 12.34s.
- `git diff --check`
- Result: passed.
- The fake-timer cleanup settles the deliberately stalled `auth.test` promise before aborting and awaiting the monitor, so an early assertion failure cannot freeze in cleanup.
- Autoreview was retried with `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local`; the local Codex review engine exited before returning structured findings, so no clean autoreview result is claimed here.

## Proof

### Exact-head controlled Slack WebClient startup proof

- Exact head: `bd1e78af217d16fcb20124042d896ec23aaf53d5`.
- Scope: production `monitorSlackProvider()` -> production `createSlackBoltApp()` -> real `@slack/bolt` App -> real `@slack/web-api` WebClient `auth.test()` -> local HTTP transport. Neither Bolt nor WebClient was mocked.
- Harness: a temporary, uncommitted `node:http` server configured through Slack WebClient's `SLACK_API_URL` endpoint hook. It accepted `POST /api/auth.test`, deliberately withheld response headers, then released the underlying response after OpenClaw reached its degraded startup path.
- Redacted command form actually run:

  ```bash
  PROOF_HEAD=bd1e78af21 \
    HTTP_PROXY= HTTPS_PROXY= http_proxy= https_proxy= ALL_PROXY= all_proxy= \
    NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost no_proxy=127.0.0.1,localhost \
    /usr/bin/timeout 90s "$(command -v node)" --import tsx \
    scratchpad/slack-startup-local-proof.mts
  ```

- Redacted transcript:

  ```text
  proof: exact-head=bd1e78af21 controlled local Slack transport
  slack-api-root: http://127.0.0.1:<redacted-port>/api/
  server: accepted POST /api/auth.test
  runtime-log: [default] slack auth.test failed at boot (slack startup auth.test timed out); explicit bot-mention detection will be disabled until restart with a valid bot token; required-mention channels will fail closed without another trusted activation signal
  runtime-log: slack http mode listening at /slack/events
  monitor: degraded startup reached http listener path elapsed=10189ms
  server: released /api/auth.test after 10191ms
  monitor: stopped cleanly after abort
  shellExit=0
  ```

- Observation: a real Slack WebClient request stalled before headers, the production 10-second boundary returned through the existing fail-closed warning path, HTTP-mode startup continued, and the monitor then stopped cleanly. The underlying WebClient request is not canceled by the caller-side timeout, so the harness explicitly released it after observing the fallback.
- Not tested: live Slack credentials, a real workspace, Slack's public API/TLS route, Socket Mode, proxy/custom CA behavior, or a real Slack outage. This is controlled local production-path transport proof, not live Slack behavior.
